papers.title: Robot Design With Neural Networks, MILP Solvers and Active Learning
papers.abstract: Central to the design of many robot systems and their controllers is solving a constrained blackbox optimization problem. This paper presents CNMA, a new method of solving this problem that is conservative in the number of potentially expensive blackbox function evaluations; allows specifying complex, even recursive constraints directly rather than as hard-to-design penalty or barrier functions; and is resilient to the non-termination of function evaluations. CNMA leverages the ability of neural networks to approximate any continuous function, their transformation into equivalent mixed integer linear programs (MILPs) and their optimization subject to constraints with industrial strength MILP solvers. A new learning-from-failure step guides the learning to be relevant to solving the constrained optimization problem. Thus, the amount of learning is orders of magnitude smaller than that needed to learn functions over their entire domains. CNMA is illustrated with the design of several robotic systems: wave-energy propelled boat, lunar lander, hexapod, cartpole, acrobot and parallel parking. These range from 6 real-valued dimensions to 36. We show that CNMA surpasses the Nelder-Mead, Gaussian and Random Search optimization methods against the metric of number of function evaluations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法通过主动学习和MILP求解器优化约束黑箱问题，可迁移到植入物设计中昂贵的仿真优化场景。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA validation, no biomedical context, no uncertainty quantification, and no demonstration on implant or biomechanics design problems.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决昂贵黑箱约束优化问题中函数评估次数多的问题。
summary_zh.method: 结合神经网络逼近、MILP求解和主动学习，逐步引导学习过程。
summary_zh.result: 在多个机器人设计任务上以更少评估次数超越Nelder-Mead等方法。
summary_zh.validation: 在6维到36维机器人系统仿真案例中验证。

summary_en.motivation: To solve constrained blackbox optimization with expensive function evaluations, the paper proposes a method that minimizes the number of calls. (abbreviated)
summary_en.method: The method, CNMA, uses neural networks to approximate the blackbox function, transforms them into MILP for constraint handling, and applies active learning to focus evaluations on relevant regions.
summary_en.result: CNMA outperforms Nelder-Mead, Gaussian processes, and random search in terms of evaluation count on various robot design problems (6-36 dimensions).
summary_en.validation: Validated on simulation cases of six robotic systems including wave-energy boat, lunar lander, hexapod, cartpole, acrobot, and parallel parking.

papers.title: Semi-supervised Batch Active Learning via Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Active learning is an effective technique for reducing the labeling cost by improving data efficiency. In this work, we propose a novel batch acquisition strategy for active learning in the setting where the model training is performed in a semi-supervised manner. We formulate our approach as a data summarization problem via bilevel optimization, where the queried batch consists of the points that best summarize the unlabeled data pool. We show that our method is highly effective in keyword detection tasks in the regime when only few labeled samples are available.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文与用户研究方向无关，不涉及FEA或替代建模。
llm.why_not_core: No FEA, no surrogate modeling, no uncertainty quantification, and no engineering optimization; it is purely ML methodology for NLP keyword detection.

summary_en.motivation: Reduce labeling cost in semi-supervised active learning
summary_en.method: Batch acquisition via bilevel optimization for data summarization

papers.title: Cold-start Active Learning through Self-supervised Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Active learning strives to reduce annotation costs by choosing the most critical examples to label. Typically, the active learning strategy is contingent on the classification model. For instance, uncertainty sampling depends on poorly calibrated model confidence scores. In the cold-start setting, active learning is impractical because of model instability and data scarcity. Fortunately, modern NLP provides an additional source of information: pre-trained language models. The pre-training loss can find examples that surprise the model and should be labeled for efficient fine-tuning. Therefore, we treat the language modeling loss as a proxy for classification uncertainty. With BERT, we develop a simple strategy based on the masked language modeling loss that minimizes labeling costs for text classification. Compared to other baselines, our approach reaches higher accuracy within less sampling iterations and computation time.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究自然语言处理中的冷启动主动学习，与FEA代理模型或生物力学优化无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses active learning for text classification using language model loss, with no relevance to surrogate modeling, finite element analysis, or biomechanical design.

summary_zh.motivation: 减少文本分类中冷启动阶段的标注成本。
summary_zh.method: 利用BERT的掩码语言模型损失作为分类不确定性的代理。
summary_zh.result: 在更少的采样迭代中达到更高准确率。
summary_zh.validation: 在NLP基准数据集上比较主动学习策略。

summary_en.motivation: To reduce annotation costs in cold-start text classification by leveraging pre-trained language models.
summary_en.method: The masked language modeling loss of BERT is used as a proxy for classification uncertainty to guide active learning.
summary_en.result: The proposed strategy achieves higher accuracy with fewer sampling iterations compared to traditional active learning baselines.
summary_en.validation: Empirical evaluation on several text classification benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Stationary Activations for Uncertainty Calibration in Deep Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a new family of non-linear neural network activation functions that mimic the properties induced by the widely-used Matérn family of kernels in Gaussian process (GP) models. This class spans a range of locally stationary models of various degrees of mean-square differentiability. We show an explicit link to the corresponding GP models in the case that the network consists of one infinitely wide hidden layer. In the limit of infinite smoothness the Matérn family results in the RBF kernel, and in this case we recover RBF activations. Matérn activation functions result in similar appealing properties to their counterparts in GP models, and we demonstrate that the local stationarity property together with limited mean-square differentiability shows both good performance and uncertainty calibration in Bayesian deep learning tasks. In particular, local stationarity helps calibrate out-of-distribution (OOD) uncertainty. We demonstrate these properties on classification and regression benchmarks and a radar emitter classification task.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了用于不确定性校准的激活函数，未涉及有限元分析或生物力学代理模型，与用户的研究方向相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA, surrogate modeling, implant design, or any biomedical simulation context; it focuses on activation functions for uncertainty calibration in general deep learning tasks.

summary_zh.motivation: 改进深度学习模型的不确定性校准，尤其是分布外样本的可靠性
summary_zh.method: 提出基于Matérn核的平稳激活函数族，拟合高斯过程的局部平稳特性
summary_zh.result: Matérn激活函数在分类、回归及雷达任务中提升了不确定性校准效果
summary_zh.validation: 在标准基准数据集和雷达发射器分类任务上测试

summary_en.motivation: To improve uncertainty calibration in deep learning models, particularly for out-of-distribution detection.
summary_en.method: Introduce a family of activation functions derived from the Matérn kernel, which induce local stationarity and link to Gaussian processes.
summary_en.result: The proposed activations yield better calibrated uncertainties and competitive performance on classification and regression benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on standard benchmarks (e.g., UCI, image datasets) and a radar emitter classification task.

papers.title: Reweighting samples under covariate shift using a Wasserstein distance criterion
papers.abstract: Considering two random variables with different laws to which we only have access through finite size iid samples, we address how to reweight the first sample so that its empirical distribution converges towards the true law of the second sample as the size of both samples goes to infinity. We study an optimal reweighting that minimizes the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measures of the two samples, and leads to an expression of the weights in terms of Nearest Neighbors. The consistency and some asymptotic convergence rates in terms of expected Wasserstein distance are derived, and do not need the assumption of absolute continuity of one random variable with respect to the other. These results have some application in Uncertainty Quantification for decoupled estimation and in the bound of the generalization error for the Nearest Neighbor Regression under covariate shift.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种基于Wasserstein距离的样本重加权方法，可用于协变量偏移下的不确定性量化，但与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计的直接关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modeling for expensive simulations, constraint handling, or biomechanics/implant design; it focuses on theoretical sample reweighting under covariate shift.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决协变量偏移下有限样本的重加权问题
summary_zh.method: 通过最小化Wasserstein距离并利用最近邻算法计算最优权重
summary_zh.result: 证明了所提方法的相合性和收敛速率

summary_en.motivation: To optimally reweight finite samples when the source and target distributions differ under covariate shift.
summary_en.method: An optimal reweighting scheme minimizing the Wasserstein distance between empirical measures, with weights expressed via nearest neighbors.
summary_en.result: Consistency and asymptotic convergence rates in expected Wasserstein distance are established.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs and asymptotic analysis without absolute continuity assumptions.

papers.title: Safe and active parameter exploration for event-triggered control
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework of learning parameter space for event-triggered control. In particular, our goal is to find a set of parameters for the event-triggered condition, such that certain specifications on safety and convergence properties are satisfied. The exploration strategy is based on the Gaussian process-based active learning, in which, for each iteration, the parameter with having the largest variance is evaluated. Moreover, we provide a theoretical analysis, so that the derived parameter space satisfies both convergence and safety. Finally, a numerical simulation is given to illustrate the effectiveness of the approach.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文针对事件触发控制参数探索，与有限元代理建模及生物力学植入物设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses event-triggered control parameter exploration, not surrogate modeling for FEA or optimization in implant mechanics; it lacks any biomedical context, FEA validation, or handling of constraints found in implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 寻找满足安全性和收敛性的事件触发控制参数集。
summary_zh.method: 基于高斯过程主动学习，每次迭代选择方差最大的参数进行评估。
summary_zh.result: 通过数值模拟验证了方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To identify parameter sets for event-triggered control that guarantee both safety and convergence properties.
summary_en.method: Gaussian process-based active learning is employed, where at each iteration the parameter with the largest variance is evaluated.
summary_en.result: Numerical simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed exploration strategy.
summary_en.validation: The method is validated through a numerical simulation case.
